tasks.title: Build artifacts: the pen canvas, live pages and ink on any artifact
tasks.description:
Spec for projects plan §5.10 (D22–D27), `.design-foundations/plans/2026-10-06-projects.md`; pixels in DESIGN.md "Artifact panel, canvas and ink"; terms in core/words. Grilled with the owner on 2026-10-13; the decision log carries his words. tsk-3 (preview comments, the canvas-panel layout) is a child of this task and folds in unchanged.

### Problem Statement

The operator thinks in diagrams and marks. On the iPad Pro with a pencil there is no way to draw something for the agent, and a drawing sent as a picture is a dead end: the agent cannot change it and send it back. Feedback on a preview is a tap on one element; a circle drawn around a region, with a word beside it, has nowhere to go. And the preview itself is a window, not a place: a questionnaire the agent sends cannot see its answers being filled in, cannot be extended as the conversation goes, and loses its state on a refresh or in a new tab.

### Solution

The preview becomes the **artifact**: a document a session made that you work in, kept by the hub, in one panel per session. Three kinds share everything: a **page** (HTML the agent wrote), a **canvas** (an Excalidraw drawing by either side) and a **preview** (a dev server shown live). A pen swipe up on the composer grows the pill into a canvas the way it grows into the recall wheel; Attach → Draw, ⌘⇧D and the panel's + open one anywhere. A canvas goes to the agent as an outline it can navigate plus a picture, and the agent draws back in skeleton elements or Mermaid; the drawing updates in place on every screen. Ink on any artifact is drawn in the overlay, anchored to the elements under it, and a radial menu at the stroke's end makes it an annotation, a comment, or an illustration. Every artifact is one Yjs document the hub syncs and persists, so a tab of its own, the iPad and the panel are the same thing, and a page the agent re-publishes morphs in place without losing what was typed.

### User Stories

1. As the operator on an iPad Pro, I want to swipe up from the composer with the pencil and get a canvas, so that I can draw what I mean without leaving the conversation.
2. As the operator, I want a finger's swipe up to keep opening the recall wheel, so that the new gesture takes nothing away.
3. As the operator on a phone, a mouse or a finger, I want Attach → Draw (and ⌘⇧D on the web) to open the same canvas, so that drawing is not pencil-only.
4. As the operator, I want the canvas to grow out of the composer the way the wheel does and keep the text field below it, so that I can draw and type in one place.
5. As the operator, I want to drag the canvas's top edge to resize it, so that it takes the room I want.
6. As the operator, I want a Dock button that sends the canvas to the side like the preview, and Undock to bring it back, so that the layout is mine.
7. As the operator on an iPad, I want my finger to pan and pinch while the pencil draws, so that drawing feels like Notes and Freeform.
8. As the operator, I want pressure in my strokes, so that the drawing looks like what I drew.
9. As the operator, I want a stroke I hold still at its end to snap to a line, arrow, rectangle, ellipse or triangle, so that diagrams are tidy without picking tools.
10. As the operator, I want the pencil's double-tap to toggle the eraser, so that the pencil's own convention works.
11. As the operator, I want shapes, arrows, text and a selection tool on the canvas, so that I can diagram, not only sketch.
12. As the operator, I want Done to fold the canvas into a chip in the composer and Send to fly it into the transcript, so that a drawing is a message like any other.
13. As the agent, I want a canvas to arrive as an outline (ids, types, text, boxes, arrow bindings) plus a picture, so that I can both see it and refer to its parts by id.
14. As the agent, I want to draw back in skeleton elements or Mermaid, so that I write the format I write best and the host fills in the rest.
15. As the agent, I want to create a canvas unprompted and edit an existing one by id, so that diagrams are mine to keep and iterate.
16. As the operator, I want the agent's edit to appear on my canvas in place, with nothing moving under my pen, so that iteration is live and calm.
17. As the operator, I want my half-drawn stroke never overwritten by the agent, so that two hands on one canvas is safe.
18. As the agent, I want a write that lands on an element the operator changed since my last read to be flagged in the result, so that I know what moved.
19. As the operator, I want a questionnaire the agent sends to notice my answers as I give them, so that I never have to say "done" field by field.
20. As the agent, I want the operator's changes delivered as one message after a short quiet, and at once while my turn is running, so that I can add questions as answers come in without a turn per click.
21. As the agent, I want to re-publish a page and have it morph in place, keeping focus, scroll and typed values, so that an update is never jarring.
22. As the operator, I want to open an artifact in a new tab and find the same tools and state, so that a bigger screen is not a disconnected preview.
23. As the operator, I want an artifact to survive closing the panel, refreshing and switching device, so that nothing is lost by accident.
24. As the operator, I want a panel per session listing its artifacts newest first, so that I can find any page, canvas or preview the session made.
25. As the agent inside a project, I want to escalate an artifact into the repository, so that work worth keeping is versioned with the project.
26. As the operator, I want to ink on any artifact with the pencil at once, with a finger still scrolling, so that marking up is as natural as reading.
27. As the operator, I want the ink to stay exactly on what I marked through scrolling, resizing and the agent's edits, so that a circle still circles the thing.
28. As the operator, I want an icon at the stroke's end whose radial menu lets me annotate, comment, illustrate or erase with one press-and-drag, so that the ink's meaning is one gesture away.
29. As the operator, I want an annotation to pin the elements under the ink with their source location, so that the agent knows what file and line I mean.
30. As the operator, I want a comment to open a thread the agent can reply to and resolve, so that feedback has a place to live.
31. As the operator, I want ignored ink to go along as a picture on the next Send, so that a doodle is never lost or in the way.
32. As the operator, I want "Send N" to send unsent pins, comments and picks as one turn, so that feedback is batched the way I give it.
33. As the operator, I want reduced motion respected (fades only) and VoiceOver to reach the canvas, the panel's list and every tool, so that the feature is usable without the gestures.
34. As the operator, I want every control 44 pt under a finger, so that the pencil and the finger both land.
35. As the agent, I want each tool to answer only what the hub stored, so that "shown" means shown.

### Implementation Decisions

- **One concept.** Artifact, with kinds page, canvas and preview; one store, one overlay, one bridge, one panel. The plan's §5.7 Svelte Flow surface is dropped; a project's artifacts are the same panel at project scope. Words: artifact, page, canvas (now a drawing), preview, pin, comment (core/words).
- **The document.** One Yjs doc per artifact. Maps: `state` (every page field by name or id plus picks, notes, dials; `data-cawco-choice` kept for custom widgets), `elements` (the canvas through y-excalidraw; element-level last-writer-wins by version and versionNonce, Excalidraw's own reconcile rule; an element being edited locally is kept), `ink` (stroke groups relative to their anchor element's box, with page coordinates, selector and source), `comments` and `pins` (tsk-3). The hub is the sync server (y-websocket protocol over the preview listener) and persists the update log in SQLite. Keys outlive revisions.
- **Agent access.** Tools read a JSON snapshot (state, pins, comments, the canvas outline, optionally a PNG) and write JSON patches applied as one Y transaction; a write on an element the person changed since the last read is applied and flagged. The `.excalidraw` file is the truth; the agent writes skeleton elements (`convertToExcalidrawElements`) or Mermaid (`@excalidraw/mermaid-to-excalidraw`). A send carries the file, the outline and the PNG through the existing `attachments`/`images` contract.
- **Live updates.** A re-published page morphs in place with idiomorph (`restoreFocus`, the active field's value kept). A canvas changes in place through the binding. A morph or remote element change waits for pointer-up and field blur. A dev-server preview keeps its own HMR.
- **Delivery.** Changes batch into one message after 3 s of quiet (`--dur-wait-grace` × 3), and go at once while the session's turn runs. "Send N" sends unsent pins, comments and picks as one turn (tsk-3).
- **Its own tab.** The dashboard's artifact route with the panel's chrome and the same doc. The overlay has one transport seam: parent window (iframe), WebKit handler (iOS), direct hub socket (own tab).
- **The panel.** The preview sheet's recipe; head with the artifact's name as the title control, Open in new tab, Dock/Undock, Comment, Reload, Close; the list newest first. `artifact_promote` writes `artifacts/<name>/` into a project's repository.
- **The canvas.** `@excalidraw/excalidraw` (MIT) in the overlay host, chrome hidden, our tool rail on house tokens; pen mode on iPad; shape recognition ours, in v1, on `--dur-press-hold`; the pencil's double-tap toggles the eraser. tldraw is out (commercial licence required in production). PencilKit is not used.
- **Entrances and motion.** Pen swipe up on the pill (touch type decides; the pencil leaves the wheel's recognizer in the app; `pointerType === "pen"` on the web); Attach → Draw; ⌘⇧D; the panel's +. The grown shape rises to the canvas with the field below; top-edge resize, floor 40 %; Dock is a shared-element flight into the panel; Done folds to a chip; Send flies the chip. Phones: Attach → Draw, full height, Dock to the drawer. DESIGN.md decides every value.
- **Ink.** An SVG layer in the page's document; strokes from Pointer Events (pen, pressure, tilt, coalesced and predicted events) rendered with perfect-freehand; a finger never inks; stroke groups anchored to the deepest containing element; the icon at the stroke's end and its four-sector radial menu (Annotate → numbered pin on the elements under the ink; Comment → pin with a thread; Illustrate → a picture; Erase); ignored ink is a picture on the next Send; re-anchoring by selector after a revision, unplaceable ink to the "moved" tray. The selection chip, its popover and selection.md are deleted (tsk-3).
- **Tools** (designed under `writing-for-agents`; CLI equivalents under the same role checks; `show_preview` and `read_choices` replaced, not aliased): `artifact_create(kind, name, html|elements|mermaid|dir|port)`, `artifact_update(id, html|patch|elements|delete|mermaid)`, `artifact_read(id, png?)` with a `since` cursor, `artifact_show(id)`, `artifact_promote(id)`; `comment_*` from tsk-3.
- **Change rules.** Cutover, no shims; no fallbacks without the owner's word; Solar duotone icons; tokens only; DESIGN.md is law.

### Testing Decisions

There are no unit tests in this repository; proof is build, lint, type-check and live checks, and a UI change is proven from the engine (computed styles, geometry, scrubbed animations, pixel diff against an approved baseline) before any picture is read.

- **One seam: the hub's artifact API** (REST for create/read/show/promote, the sync endpoint for the live doc, the MCP tools over it). Every behaviour is observable there: a field answered in a page shows up in the doc; an agent patch shows up in the page; a stroke group lands with its anchor; a re-publish keeps focus and values; a tool answers what the hub stored.
- **Driven through the existing probe kit** (`scripts/probe-kit/specs`, playwright-core and webkit-caw) against the real dashboard with a real page under the overlay, asserting on the hub's read of the doc and on engine geometry; the MCP tools through the MCP bridge script (prior art: the admin-gating probe).
- **iOS:** the simulator probe pattern of `probe-ios-composer.ts` (it reads the composer's DEBUG swipe log) extended to the pen swipe's decisions and the morph's frames (layer `speed = 0`, `timeOffset`, presentation values); the web view's content is the same overlay, proven once on the web seam.
- **The live check is the owner's,** once, on the deployed product: a canvas drawn with the pencil on the iPad reaches the agent as an outline and a picture; the agent's edit shows on the iPad without a reload; a form the agent re-publishes keeps what was typed; ink stays on its element through a scroll and an agent edit.

### Out of Scope

Mac Catalyst work; awareness cursors and multi-user presence; a drawing engine of our own; tldraw; two-way sync of artifacts to outside tools.

### Further Notes

- Sources for every library decision are in the plan's §10 (tldraw licence, Excalidraw MIT and pen mode, reconcile rule, mermaid-to-excalidraw, Yjs and y-websocket, y-excalidraw, idiomorph, WebKit pen Pointer Events, coalesced and predicted events, why not PencilKit).
- Build order that keeps each slice landable: (1) the artifact store and sync, the panel listing existing previews and pages as artifacts, `show_preview`/`read_choices` cut over to the tools; (2) pages: field tracking, batched delivery, idiomorph re-publish, the own-tab route; (3) the canvas: engine, entrances, morph, Dock, outline/PNG send, agent writes; (4) ink and the radial menu, with tsk-3's pins and comments; (5) shape recognition and the iPad pen rules; (6) `artifact_promote`. Each slice ships with its probe spec.
- A design preview for the owner's pick (the morph, the tool rail, the radial menu) is built by an Opus leaf from the dashboard's real components on a mock route before the canvas slice is built, per the fleet's rule; the UX fit comes from a Fable advisor briefed with the file, a screenshot, the requirement and the ask.

tasks.description:
Found 2026-10-13: the Fable session's delegate d9555b0d was queued behind owns overlaps and its parent could not withdraw or re-scope it. `stop_delegate` resolves only sessions (delegation-actions.ts stopDelegate ~1550, resolveDelegate ~845), and a queued delegate has none yet. work-items.ts `unqueue` (~1718: drop the row, publish the chip's removal) runs only when the parent is gone or the start throws. `delegate_list` (all) doesn't show queued delegates either. The orchestrator dropped the queued_work_items row by hand, leaving a ghost tray chip until the hub restarted.

Also found the same day: work items stay `running` forever when their session can never finish them. On obelisk, ed1435a2 "Run sleep probe 4" and 7b16852b "Run sleep probe 8" (2026-10-05) point at instance ids 4c24ed0b and 5073a7fe, which have no instances row at all. Seven more (d3de5c61, c4bfc660, 82de73f7, 5a7110fa, 37a7c004, 727ae77d, f3fca633) belong to sessions asleep since 2026-09-30 to 10-05, with no finish_item and no wait set.

Build:
- `stop_delegate` given a queued delegate's id (full, or its 8-character prefix) withdraws it through `unqueue`, only for the caller's own queue rows (parent_instance_id) or a project it leads. It answers: Withdrew your queued delegate “<title>” (<id8>): it never started, so it has no session or workspace.
- `delegate_list` lists the caller's queued delegates as state `queued`, with queued_at and what holds it: the live item and the glob that overlaps (the ownsBlocker result).
- Update the stop_delegate tool description in delegation-tools.ts to say it also withdraws a queued delegate.
- A work item whose session row no longer exists ends as failed with "its session is gone", at hub start and whenever a session row is deleted. Its parent is told, as for any failure.
- A work item whose session sleeps with no turn, no wait and no finish_item for longer than the hub's idle timeout: decide from the code what the parent was already told when that turn ended. If the parent got a "turn complete" report, it owns the decision and the item stays. If nothing told the parent, tell it now. Report which case these seven are.
Do it after tsk-4 slice 1 lands: that slice owns delegation-tools.ts and delegation-actions.ts.

tasks.title: Share the Mac between leaves: one build and simulator slot for everyone
tasks.description:
Found 2026-10-13 13:05: the owner's Mac reached a load average of 675. Four Mac leaves ran at once, each booting its own iOS Simulator (236 simulator-runtime processes), plus two Xcode builds. One of those builds was a direct `xcodebuild` in a leaf's clone, outside build-both.sh's slot. The Mac agent then answered the hub late ("unrouted reply … kind=control_result machine=271a214a"), and the fleet skill push of the patched unlazy never reached the Mac.

Today:
- apps/apple/scripts/build-both.sh serializes builds through `shlock` on `$ROOT/.locks/.machine` (lines 131-145).
- ROOT differs by caller. Inside a workspace it is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/cawco-apple` (the shared workspace cache, `~/.cawco/workspace-cache/xdg/cawco-apple`). From the orchestrator's SSH it is `~/build/cawco-apple`. So TestFlight and orchestrator builds don't share the lock with workspace builds.
- Nothing bounds simulators: every live proof boots its own, and leaves also run xcodebuild directly.

Build:
1. One lock folder for every caller: the workspace cache path, which the SSH side can write too.
2. `apps/apple/scripts/mac-slot.sh`, a Mac-wide slot every Apple leaf uses for anything outside build-both.sh: `mac-slot.sh build -- <cmd…>` and `mac-slot.sh sim -- <cmd…>`.
   - The build slot is the same lock build-both.sh holds.
   - The sim slot holds at most 2 simulators booted machine-wide.
   - It boots the simulator for the command, hands it the UDID in an env var, and shuts it down and deletes it when the command ends or its caller goes, by the same heartbeat-and-process-group pattern build-both.sh uses.
3. Every Apple brief already names build-both.sh. Add mac-slot.sh to the probe-kit Apple docs and to the brief template the orchestrator uses.

Proof on the Mac:
- three concurrent `mac-slot.sh sim` callers: the third waits until one ends, and the simulators are deleted afterwards;
- a direct-build caller waits behind a running build-both.sh;
- killing a caller mid-run frees its slot and deletes its simulator.

- a caller killed mid-run frees its slot and its simulator is deleted

result.report:
## Root cause
The failure ("37ms … our code 0ms") was the engine. Headless WPE composites every frame of the open in software GL: Mesa llvmpipe runs one thread per core ("The default value is the number of CPU cores present", https://docs.mesa3d.org/envvars.html) and a frame waits for the slowest thread.
- At rest the page composites nothing and never drops a frame.
- An open costs about 3s of compositing CPU, against about 80ms more on the main thread.
- A blank page's frames stall to 63ms quiet and 225ms under load.
- LP_NUM_THREADS set to 1 or 4 does not cure it.
- The page's own work in wall time also stretches with load: a 10ms Svelte flush took 67ms.

## Changes (rebased onto main: ca8b2386, a4ea1d95, 626061fb, d8681010, a1ab4ae9)
1. **New kit instrument, `scripts/probe-kit/cpu.ts` + `cpu-worker.ts`.** It reads the WebKit web process's main-thread CPU per frame interval from schedstat ("time spent on the cpu (in nanoseconds)", https://docs.kernel.org/scheduler/sched-stats.html), sampled every 0.25ms on a worker.
   - WebKit's 1ms-floored page clock (Performance.cpp `timePrecision { 1_ms }`, `std::floor`) is aligned to the sampler by bounding round trips.
   - Each window is bracketed by grain plus kernel tick (CONFIG_HZ, read from the kernel config) and capped at the interval as the page reads it, so it is never charged more than the old check read.
   - The web process is named by dominance over the other descendant processes during a busy page task.
   - Raster (SkiaCPUWorker) and compositing CPU are reported per open.
   - `attribute` also times setInterval callbacks and `on…` handlers.
2. **webkit-caw:** the 25ms limit is unchanged and now applies to the page's main-thread CPU per interval. A new assertion checks that the rehearsal ran unseen.
3. **Product: GlassCard's unseen first open is now a whole rehearsal.** The card opens, grows, shuts and folds once after load, invisible and inert, with focus left in place.
   - Its join is its own (`rehearsalJoined`). It arms the morph and never touches the shared `barGlass.joined`; touching it had broke the caw-notices bench's seam, fixed in 626061fb.
   - A real open during the rehearsal ends it and takes the join over.
   - `quiet` was removed from hang.ts and HangCard. It was the old warm-up's alone; main's new grow and fold no longer read it.
   - Bisect for the cold work: inert, grow, three placings, the smile clip and a join layer did nothing. A keyboard open, or a full grow with the join armed, did. The cold work was the open with the join armed, not anything drawn.

## First press, before and after
- Before: 21–28ms of main-thread CPU on a quiet machine (later presses ≤15).
- After: 14–21ms. On a1ab4ae9: 14ms alone and 14ms in the full run.

## Proof
- 30ms of fixed work reads 31.1ms of CPU quiet and 33ms with 64 busy loops, while its wall time reads 64–68ms.
- The check fails on injected script (38–45ms, named) and counts a reflow injected without script.
- Rehearsal check: 1 drawn-out state, 0 visible, glass joined in 0.
- svelte-check 0 errors; biome and tsc clean.

## Acceptance (on a1ab4ae9)
- `bun scripts/probe-kit/run.ts web webkit-caw` → ALL PASS (heaviest 14ms of CPU).
- Full web run → webkit-caw: all three PASS (heaviest 14ms).
- The full run's other failures are not this change's. hang's baseline diffs reproduce identically on pristine origin/main 05a4010a: caw/machines/jump desk 190/188px, caw-staged 15540px, session-card and tab-menu sizes. 08a00d40 changed the visuals without new baselines.

tasks.title: Decide what an early cross-organization account move does, from the compaction benchmark
tasks.description:
On 10-25 at 07:05 the hub moved the orchestrator session from jude@petralab.ai to bewinxed@gmail.com about 40 minutes before jude was forecast to run out (07:45). The cache was warm, and five minutes earlier the hub had decided it would stay. The move happened because the owner was watching: at-limit.ts rule 7 drops the free wait for a watched session, and rule 8 moves a watched session across organizations when the cold re-read is under the 600k floor. It moved whole and re-read 479k tokens cold ($3.83). A move compacts only at 600k or more, and never at a forecast (`compact: !carries && input.cause !== "refused-credential" && input.cause !== "forecast" && … reported >= policy.moveWholeUnderK * 1000`). Compacting first on the warm account would have cost about a tenth of that.

The owner's words: "not sure why we didn't compact here before moving on or if this move was necessary now", then on the choice: "finish the benchmark first, add this as a task".

This waits on the compaction benchmark (design 50b8e3cc, harness aa8e5136, finished by the benchmark run task). Then decide, against his account strategy: compact on the warm account before a cross-organization move, wait for the limit, or keep today's rule. Bring it to him with the benchmark's numbers.
